about.title: Orange Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a death in Orange is caused by someone else's carelessness, the family left behind has to make decisions at the hardest possible moment. Six people died in traffic collisions here in 2025, among 819 injury crashes recorded citywide. Some occurred on Tustin Street or Chapman Avenue; others involved SR-55 southbound and SR-22 westbound, the corridors with the highest public-record collision counts. Each figure represents an Orange County household continuing without a parent, partner, or child. California treats wrongful death as a civil matter, separate from any criminal case. Standing goes first to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children, then to certain dependents and heirs. A claim may seek funeral and burial expenses, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and shorter when a government entity is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Orange families, at no charge, with an independent attorney who works on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Orange Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney we connect you with can tell you plainly where your family stands.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a city, county, or state agency is involved. Getting an attorney involved early protects that timeline.

items.title: Every recoverable loss accounted for
items.desc: A claim can cover funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. An independent attorney can help make sure nothing is overlooked, with no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on SR-55 in Orange. Does it matter that a freeway was involved?
items.answer: It can. If a public agency's design, maintenance, or vehicle played a role, California requires a government claim to be filed far sooner than the general two-year wrongful death deadline. Freeway and arterial crashes along SR-55, SR-22, Tustin Street, or Chapman Avenue can also involve several drivers and insurers. An attorney can sort out who is responsible and which deadlines apply.

items.question: The driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death action is a civil case brought by the family and runs separately from any criminal prosecution handled by the Orange County District Attorney. The two can proceed at the same time, and a civil claim does not depend on a conviction. Evidence from the criminal case may still be useful.

items.question: I am a sibling of the person who died. Can I bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Standing goes first to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children. If none exist, certain other heirs may qualify, and people who were financially dependent on the deceased may also have a claim in specific circumstances. Because eligibility depends on your family's situation, it is worth having an independent attorney review it. LawProactive can arrange that conversation at no cost.
